reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / standard immunology references
clinicalPearls: Hyper-IgE syndrome is a group of primary immunodeficiencies characterised by markedly elevated serum IgE, recurrent skin and lung infections, and often connective tissue or skeletal abnormalities
The classic autosomal dominant form results from dominant-negative STAT3 mutations, while autosomal recessive forms (for example DOCK8 deficiency) show overlapping but distinct features
The infection pattern is dominated by Staphylococcus aureus skin abscesses that may be surprisingly non-inflamed ('cold' abscesses) and recurrent pneumonias that can leave pneumatoceles
Chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis and other fungal infections are common, reflecting impaired Th17-mediated immunity in the STAT3 form
DOCK8 deficiency is distinguished by severe cutaneous viral infections, food allergies, eosinophilia, and a high risk of malignancy
Non-immune features of the STAT3 form include a characteristic coarse facial appearance, retained primary teeth, hyperextensible joints, scoliosis, and a tendency to bone fractures
Serum IgE is often very high but does not correlate tightly with disease activity, and eosinophilia is frequent

Management centres on long-term antistaphylococcal and antifungal prophylaxis, aggressive treatment of infections, and skin care; haematopoietic stem cell transplantation can correct the recessive DOCK8 form
reference.pathophysiology: Hyper-IgE syndromes arise from defects in signalling pathways that govern T-helper cell differentiation and epithelial immunity. In the autosomal dominant form, dominant-negative mutations in STAT3 impair the development of Th17 cells and the response to several cytokines, reducing antimicrobial peptide production at skin and mucosal surfaces and blunting the acute inflammatory response, which explains the 'cold' abscesses. STAT3 also influences tissue remodelling and skeletal biology, accounting for the connective tissue, dental, and bony features. Autosomal recessive forms such as DOCK8 deficiency disrupt cytoskeletal function and lymphocyte survival, producing profound susceptibility to cutaneous viruses and severe allergic disease. Dysregulated IgE production and eosinophilia are shared consequences of the altered T-cell cytokine milieu.
additionalDifferentials: Severe atopic dermatitis with recurrent skin infection
DOCK8 deficiency and other combined immunodeficiencies
Cystic fibrosis (recurrent pneumonia with structural lung change)
Omenn syndrome and other conditions with eosinophilia and high IgE
additionalInvestigations: Serum IgE level and eosinophil count
Genetic testing for STAT3, DOCK8, and related genes
Lymphocyte subset analysis and Th17 cell enumeration where available
Clinical scoring (for example an NIH-type score) to gauge probability of the STAT3 form
Chest imaging to detect pneumatoceles, bronchiectasis, and fungal colonisation
Skeletal and dental assessment for fractures, scoliosis, and retained teeth
redFlags: Recurrent or severe deep-seated infections, including 'cold' abscesses and pneumonia with cavitation, warranting urgent immunological workup
Aspergillus or other fungal infection colonising pneumatoceles, risking invasive disease or haemorrhage
Severe disseminated viral skin infection in suspected DOCK8 deficiency
New or accelerating malignancy, particularly in the recessive form
Vascular aneurysms in the STAT3 form
reference.prognosis: With sustained prophylaxis and prompt treatment of infections, many patients with the autosomal dominant STAT3 form reach adulthood, though pulmonary complications and vascular aneurysms remain important causes of morbidity. The autosomal recessive DOCK8 form carries a poorer outlook because of severe viral infections and malignancy, and haematopoietic stem cell transplantation offers the best chance of cure.
pitfalls: Attributing recurrent staphylococcal abscesses to simple atopic dermatitis and missing the underlying immunodeficiency
Assuming a very high IgE alone confirms the diagnosis, since it is neither fully sensitive nor specific
Overlooking the skeletal, dental, and vascular features that distinguish the STAT3 form
Failing to recognise DOCK8 deficiency as a transplantable condition with a different management path
Not monitoring pneumatoceles for secondary fungal infection
